extra.message: User-supplied query parameter 'username' is interpolated directly into the SQL string f'SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = "{username}";' and passed to run_sql_query() which executes it via aiosqlite. An attacker can break out of the quoted string (e.g. '" OR 1=1; -- ') to read or manipulate the entire database. This is a classic SQL injection.

The PUT /user endpoint builds an INSERT statement via f-string interpolation of attacker-controlled User fields (user.name, user.username, user.address, user.email, user.contact) and executes it with run_sql_query(query, commit=True). Any of these JSON body fields can contain quotes to inject arbitrary SQL, enabling data theft, modification, or stacked-query attacks.

The DELETE /user endpoint interpolates the 'username' query parameter directly into f'DELETE FROM users WHERE username = "{username}";' and executes it with commit=True. An attacker can inject SQL (e.g. '" OR 1=1; -- ') to delete all rows or run arbitrary statements.

The DELETE /user endpoint interpolates user.address directly (unquoted) into f'DELETE FROM users WHERE address = {user.address};' and executes it with commit=True. Because the value is not quoted or parameterized, arbitrary SQL can be injected through the address field of the request body.

The POST /find endpoint takes the raw JSON request body (await request.json()) and passes it directly as the filter to MontyDB users.find(query) via get_nosql_users(). An attacker can supply query operators such as {'id': {'$in': [1,2]}} or {'username': {'$gt': ''}} to bypass filters and enumerate or extract all user records (NoSQL operator injection).

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: The DELETE /user endpoint performs destructive deletion of user records from both the Mongo-style and SQLite databases without any authentication or authorization check. Any unauthenticated remote client can delete arbitrary users (or, combined with the SQL injection on line 231/235, wipe the entire table).

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The POST /reset endpoint deletes the SQLite database file (os.remove) and removes the entire NoSQL database directory (shutil.rmtree) with no authentication or authorization. Any unauthenticated remote attacker can destroy all application data at will, causing denial of service and data loss.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: User passwords are hashed with unsalted MD5 (md5(user.password.encode()).hexdigest()) before storage. MD5 is fast and broken for password storage; hashes can be brute-forced or looked up in rainbow tables trivially. The same weak hashing is used for seed data at line 113.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: run_sql_query() returns raw rows (return {'users': _data}) including the password column (MD5 hashes) whenever a query yields multiple results. Since /select exposes this helper directly to clients, a multi-row result (trivially obtained via the SQL injection on line 182 or a username matching multiple rows) discloses password hashes of all users.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
